summary: Deschutes NF lookout on Green Ridge near Sisters, Oregon: a tree platform, then a 1940 timber tower that sources date differently; gone by 1965.

facts.design: Treated timber tower with a 7x7-foot steel cab (register); the L-4 cab appears only in a 1944 history-page entry
facts.status_note: Gone by 1965 per the register and firelookout.com; firelookout.com also says the 70-foot crow's nest is still there

staffing.status: lookout Charles Lewis in July 1940; one fire reported from the station in 1959; no end-of-staffing date in these sources

events.note: Firelookout.com dates the 70-foot crow's nest to 1935; the register gives the tree platform no date
Five Fingered Sentinal butte chosen for a new lookout, per a 1939 Bend Bulletin item
85-foot treated timber tower with steel cab and a cabin replaced the tree platform, per the register and firelookout.com

Six-acre hunter fire directly west of the lookout, extinguished by forest service employees (October 1941)
History page lists a 76-foot treated timber tower with a 14x14 L-4 cab, a couple miles north of the tree lookout; conflicts with the 1940 tower
One fire reported from the station during the 1959 fire season
Gone by 1965 per the register and firelookout.com

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 85 feet (about 25.9 m) for the 1940 timber tower; the history page gives 76 feet (23.2 m) for a 1944 tower. The record keeps 23.2 m, the brief's value, which matches the history page only. The story gives both heights.

The register and firelookout.com date the timber tower to 1940. The history page dates a 76-foot tower to 1944, north of the tree lookout. The sources do not show whether these are one structure or two, so the story reports both.

The register describes a 70-foot tree platform; the history page describes a 90-foot pine with a six-foot platform located southwest of the later site. Both are reported; the register's 70 feet is not confirmed.
Firelookout.com says the 70-foot crow's nest is still there; the register says the lookout was gone by 1965. No source describes the site now, so the record keeps status gone.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 23.2 (76 ft) matches only the 1944 history-page tower; the register and firelookout.com say 85 ft (about 25.9 m). The brief's 1940 build date matches the register, not the history page's 1944. The brief's L-4 design code appears only on the 1944 cab, so design is recorded as the register's steel cab. A Recreation.gov listing for a separate Green Ridge Lookout (built in the 1960s) is not tied to this site by any source read, and visitors could confuse them. A mapcarta listing called the site a ruin and a Facebook group post mentioned a 1965 last season; neither was read in full, so neither is used. Access is omitted because no source describes it.
